items.title: ADR: Bedrock Lease And Fencing Contract

requirements.statement: With Bedrock-backed shared storage, a keyed fleet shall rebalance across connected nodes while preserving deterministic ownership, per-key state, and cluster stats.
After a Bedrock-backed handoff, terminating the current owner node shall allow the surviving node to thaw the latest acknowledged singleton state from Bedrock and continue serving the key.
Restarting a node against the same Bedrock-backed storage path shall allow the manager to recover previously acknowledged singleton state.
A manager using the Bedrock adapter shall be able to hand off a singleton key across connected nodes while preserving state through shared Bedrock storage.
After a Bedrock-backed handoff completes, the old owner node shall not retain a live local singleton for the migrated key.
The Fly multi-region guide shall document a concrete multi-region drill for one logical Jido.Cluster.InstanceManager with shared storage and DNS-based discovery.
The multi-region guide shall describe recovery in terms of continued keyed availability, owner continuity, cluster continuity, and migration plus recovery telemetry.
With shared storage, a key shall remain serviceable after its owner node is terminated and recovered on a surviving node, and the recovery path shall emit observable recovery telemetry.
Lease acquisition requests shall be represented as typed claims that capture claimant identity, requested TTL, and renewal cadence for one `{manager, key}` pair.
Every lease acquisition shall issue a typed fence token that monotonically orders claim epochs and identifies the active holder for stale-writer rejection.
Durable lease records shall encode holder identity, issuance, expiry, cadence, and a fence token whose holder, lease id, and epoch match the lease record.
Lease and claim cadence shall require `renew_interval_ms < ttl_ms`.
The `{:bedrock_lease, ...}` coordination backend shall normalize into a typed lease backend config with explicit repo, prefix, TTL, renew cadence, clock skew budget, and retry backoff.
The application shall start a dynamic supervisor that hosts manager instances started at runtime.
The getting-started guide shall show the dependency, minimal manager setup, keyed routing, and storage-selection guidance for connected-node usage.
Both the legacy JidoCluster namespace and the preferred Jido.Cluster namespace shall expose connected_nodes/0 for the visible cluster view.
Optional cluster formation shall support libcluster topologies and dns_cluster discovery when those dependencies are available.
Raw peer-started Erlang nodes shall be able to connect and execute the package topology helpers once the project code path is loaded.
Cluster manager config shall normalize replication settings into a typed Jido.Cluster.Replication struct with validated policy fields.
Ownership, runtime summary, and runtime snapshot structs shall describe the same primary/standby pair and expose enough metadata to compare competing views during handoff, failover, and heal.

Placement, ownership, runtime summary, and runtime snapshot contracts shall use consistent role, epoch, and sequence semantics, where role is per-runtime, epoch orders ownership changes, and sequence orders acknowledged replicated updates.
Cluster topology views shall carry the visible node set, elected leader, quorum result, and observation timestamp as typed data.
With `{:bedrock_lease, ...}` coordination, one island shall acquire one logical owner for a key while other islands are rejected until the lease expires or is released.
After lease expiry, another island shall be able to acquire the same key, thaw shared durable state, and continue execution.
Releasing a lease shall allow another island to reacquire the same key without same-key dual ownership.
Repeated manager-routed operations from the current holder shall renew the active lease before expiry.
After another island acquires a key, the stale previous holder shall reject manager-routed operations and stop any local runtime for that key.
When the primary disappears, the standby shall promote using the latest acknowledged replicated state for the key.
Planned live transfer shall move primary ownership without resetting the logical agent state.
A clustered key shall maintain one primary runtime and at most one standby runtime across the connected replica set.
After a soft-owner split heals, the runtime shall converge back to one primary and one standby without duplicating ownership.
Acknowledged call and cast operations shall synchronize standby state before the primary reports success.
The preferred Jido.Cluster.Error namespace shall expose validation_error, config_error, and execution_error helpers.
Error helper calls shall return typed exceptions for invalid input, configuration failures, and runtime execution failures.
In live-transfer mode, manager-routed get, call, and cast operations shall ensure the primary and standby replica set exists before signaling the logical agent.
Clustered agent access shall route by manager and key so the current owner can change without making raw pids the stability boundary.
owner_node and stats shall reflect the current distributed placement and visible primary ownership for the cluster view.
`get` and `lookup` shall return observational pids for the current primary rather than a durable cross-node identity for the logical key.
The package README shall state that jido_cluster is alpha-quality and not ready for production use.
The package shall target connected-BEAM keyed agent ownership, routing, and conservative rebalancing as its primary runtime scope.
The preferred public namespace shall be Jido.Cluster.* while legacy JidoCluster.* modules may remain as compatibility shims.
For connected_beam coordination with partition_policy :freeze, cluster availability shall depend on the visible node set satisfying min_quorum_nodes.
In a three-node split with quorum requirement 2, the minority side shall freeze while the majority side can recover ownership.
A two-node split with quorum requirement 2 shall freeze both sides, reject new clustered work, and stop local ownership.
Rebalance work shall run only on the deterministic leader while the cluster is considered available for that manager.
Shared-backend rebalancing shall migrate at most max_migrations_per_tick keys during one tick.
The preferred public rebalancer namespace shall expose trigger and trigger_sync operations for manager-scoped migration ticks.
Rebalance attempts shall skip non-shared backends and emit skipped migration telemetry instead of trying to move keys.
The Bedrock adapter shall scan thread entry prefixes with a strict upper bound so prefixed entry keys are fully loaded and deleted.
Storage adapters shall support checkpoint create, read, and delete operations for clustered agent state.
Adapters that expose optimistic concurrency shall reject stale expected_rev writes with a conflict result.
The getting-started guide shall describe the intended tradeoff between ETS, Mnesia, Bedrock, and Postgres storage backends.
The preferred Jido.Cluster.Storage namespace shall expose the clustered adapter surface while delegating behavior to the legacy implementation modules.
Storage adapters shall append, load, and delete thread data while reconstructing thread revision and ordered entries.
ETS-backed storage shall be classified as non-shared so automatic migrations do not assume cross-node durability.
Mnesia, Bedrock, and Postgres cluster adapters shall be classified as shared backends for migration and failover behavior.
Unknown adapters shall fall back to opts[:shared] when determining whether the backend is migration-safe.
The connected cluster view shall include Node.self/0 and remain sorted deterministically.
Placement shall use rendezvous hashing to produce a deterministic primary/standby ordering for a given manager, key, and node set.
Leader selection and quorum evaluation shall be derived only from the visible connected node set for a given topology view.
The repository shall include a .spec/AGENTS.md that gives local operating guidance for agents working inside the .spec workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/decisions/README.md that explains when durable ADRs belong in the workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/README.md that explains purpose, layout, and workflow.
When planning and verification run, the workspace shall generate .spec/state.json containing indexed subjects, indexed decisions, and verification state.

given: a lease backend config
a claim request
a fence token
a durable lease record
then: the resulting data preserves cadence constraints and stale-writer fencing metadata
when: each value is built through its public constructor

given: two raw :peer nodes with the project code path loaded
then: both nodes appear in the connected cluster view
when: one node connects to the other and calls the topology helper

given: representative config, placement, ownership, snapshot, and topology inputs
then: the resulting values preserve typed role, epoch, sequence, and quorum metadata
when: the structs are constructed through their public constructors

given: a key whose desired owner changes after a new node joins
then: the new primary preserves the prior logical agent state
when: the rebalancer performs a planned live transfer

given: a replicated key with acknowledged state on the standby
then: the standby promotes and continues from the latest acknowledged state
when: the primary node terminates

given: two connected nodes running the same ephemeral clustered manager
then: one primary runtime and one standby runtime are created for that key
when: a caller gets a keyed agent for the first time

given: a soft-owner split where the standby promoted during temporary isolation
then: the key converges back to one primary and one standby with a consistent healed ownership view and preserved acknowledged sequence
when: cluster connectivity heals and both runtimes can compare ownership state again

given: a primary and standby runtime already exist for a key
then: both runtimes reflect the same replicated state before the caller sees success
when: a caller performs acknowledged call and cast operations

given: a clustered manager that starts on one node and later gains a second node
then: the logical agent remains available and preserves prior state
when: ownership rebalances to the new owner

given: two connected nodes running the same ephemeral clustered manager
then: both callers route through one logical singleton with a synchronized primary and standby
when: callers access the same key from either node

given: two connected nodes and many distinct keys
then: primary ownership is distributed across both nodes by key
when: the keys are accessed through the clustered manager

given: a single connected node running an ephemeral clustered manager
then: the manager exposes one stable logical singleton lifecycle for that key
when: a caller gets, calls, casts, and inspects a keyed agent through the manager

given: a three-node cluster running a shared-backend manager with quorum 2
then: the isolated minority freezes and the majority can recover the key
when: one node becomes isolated from the other two

given: a two-node cluster running a shared-backend manager with quorum 2
then: both sides freeze during the split and the logical key can resume after heal
when: the nodes disconnect and later reconnect

given: a manager using a local ETS backend and a topology mismatch after a node joins
then: the key stays put and skipped migration telemetry is emitted
when: the leader triggers a rebalance tick

given: a manager using a shared backend and multiple candidate keys that want to move
then: only one key migrates during that tick
when: the leader triggers one rebalance tick

given: any of the supported storage adapters
then: the adapter preserves checkpoint payloads and reconstructed thread state
when: checkpoints and threads are written, read back, and deleted

given: a Bedrock-backed thread written under a shared prefix
then: all prefixed entries are included in the operation range
when: the thread is loaded or deleted through the adapter

given: a fixed manager, key, and node list
then: the same primary and standby ordering is returned consistently
when: placement and replica nodes are derived multiple times

given: an explicit visible node list and a quorum threshold
then: the view records the sorted nodes, leader, and quorum result for that input
when: a topology view is built
